market_context.summary: Bain & Company estimates India's e-retail market at $65-66 billion of gross merchandise value in 2025 (up 19-21%) with 290-300 million online shoppers, and expects $170-180 billion by 2030. Quick commerce already carries 16-17% of that GMV ($10-11 billion in 2025, doubling annually since 2023), led by Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart, with Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now scaling fast. Redseer puts online beauty and personal care at about ₹52,000 crore in 2025, 2.4 times its 2022 level, and says quick commerce's share of it rose from about 2% to about 16% in three years. Motilal Oswal credits Nykaa with roughly 27% of online beauty and personal care but notes that personal care is 'FMCG driven' and price-sensitive, so the horizontal marketplaces (press-reported analyst estimates put Flipkart at 50-60% and Amazon at 25-30% of e-commerce GMV) and quick commerce matter most for mass-market hair, skin and oral care. No regulator-verified market shares exist for these platforms; every share quoted here is an analyst or third-party estimate.

key_facts.fact: India's e-retail market reached $65-66 billion of GMV in 2025 (growth 19-21%), with 290-300 million online shoppers; forecast $170-180 billion by 2030.
Quick commerce accounts for 16-17% of India's e-retail GMV, reached $10-11 billion in 2025 after doubling annually since 2023, and is expected to reach $65-70 billion by the end of the decade.

India's online beauty and personal-care market grew from about ₹21,000 crore in 2022 to about ₹52,000 crore in 2025; quick commerce's share of online beauty and personal care rose from about 2% to about 16%, and the category is the second-largest in quick commerce after grocery.

Motilal Oswal (December 2025): Nykaa has a roughly 27% share of India's online beauty and personal-care market; online was 20% of the total category in FY25 (about USD 5 billion) and is expected to reach 34% by FY30; 'quick commerce could wrestle away some market share in personal care' because assortments are 'standardized and FMCG driven'.
key_facts.source_name: Motilal Oswal Financial Services (PDF hosted by Business Standard)

key_facts.fact: Inc42 reports that Flipkart holds 'a 50-60% market share on a gross merchandise value (GMV) basis' with 220 million monthly active users. This is a press-reported analyst estimate, not a verified share.
key_facts.source_name: Press and broker estimates via Inc42

key_facts.fact: A NewsBytes item, read only as a search-result summary because the page returned HTTP 403, attributes the Flipkart estimate to ICICI Securities and adds Amazon India at 25-30% and Meesho at about 10% of e-commerce GMV.

Datum Intelligence daily-order estimates for August 2026: Blinkit 3.4-3.6 million, Zepto 2.4-2.6 million, Swiggy Instamart 1.3-1.45 million, Flipkart Minutes 0.9-1.0 million, Amazon Now 0.6-0.7 million, BigBasket 0.5-0.6 million; the six platforms together handled about 9.5 million orders a day.

Redseer's 'India BPC 2030' report as cited by Business Today: the beauty and personal-care market is about $23 billion (FY2025) and projected at about $40 billion by 2030; online is roughly one-fifth of spending; quick commerce contributes around 15% of online beauty sales today and could reach nearly 40% by 2030.
IBEF's industry profile reports 1,092.79 million internet subscribers in India at the end of March 2026 (subscribers, not unique users; the underlying source is not named on the page).

ranking_method_note: Scores follow the brief's rubric exactly: five criteria scored 1-5, weighted 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.20 / 0.15 / 0.20, summed and rounded to two decimals; rank 1 is the highest weighted score. Ties are broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach; where a tie still remained, brand_competitor_coverage, data_integration_feasibility, ecommerce_significance and finally alphabetical order were used (an addition, because the rubric is silent). estimated_market_importance reflects overall importance in the country's online retail (tier_1 = market-shaping, tier_2 = significant, tier_3 = niche or emerging), not category relevance, which is captured separately in beauty_relevance. Scoring anchors: ecommerce_significance 5 = market-shaping leader, 4 = top-tier national player, 3 = significant category or regional player, 2 = niche or emerging. consumer_reach: 5 = 150 million or more India web visits in October 2026 (Semrush) or 200 million or more annual transacting users; 4 = 50-150 million visits, or a 100M+ Google Play install band backed by evidence of a large transacting base (orders, GMV or monthly users); 3 = 10-50 million visits or a 50M+ install band; 2 = 3-10 million visits; 1 = below 3 million. India is app-first, so web visits understate reach; Google Play install bands and company order or user metrics are shown alongside. Install bands are cumulative and include inactive users. brand_competitor_coverage is an evidence-graded judgement based on how many checklist brands were confirmed on the platform's own pages, sitemaps or app-store listing and how deep the ranges were; platforms that could not be checked receive a neutral 3 and are marked UNVERIFIED. Checklist used for India: Dove, Pantene, L'Oréal Paris, Garnier, Head & Shoulders, Nivea, Vaseline, Colgate, Sensodyne, Himalaya, Dabur, Parachute, Mamaearth. data_integration_feasibility: 5 = documented public partner API plus accessible public pages, 4 = documented API with gated scope, 3 = no API but public pages or sitemaps accessible, 2 = no API and app-centric or bot-protected pages. The formula rewards reach and data access, so the two horizontal marketplaces rank above Nykaa even though Nykaa has the largest estimated share of online beauty; quick-commerce platforms score low on data access because prices and availability vary by dark store and are visible only in-app. These reservations are recorded in the relevant priority_rationale fields.
